title: Auditory system, middle ear cavity and cochlear apparatus

steps.tx: The **middle ear cavity** or tympanic cavity is an air-filled space within the petrous temporal bone. The tympanic membrane forms its lateral wall. The promontory, oval window and round window form its medial wall. The roof is the thin tegmen tympani separating it from the middle cranial fossa. The floor separates it from the internal jugular vein. The anterior wall features the auditory tube.

steps.tx: Three **auditory ossicles** bridge the middle ear to transfer sound energy from air to fluid. The malleus attaches to the tympanic membrane umbo. The incus acts as an intermediate lever. The stapes footplate attaches to the oval window membrane. The area ratio of tympanic membrane to stapes footplate together with ossicular lever action amplifies sound pressure twenty-fold, overcoming the high acoustic impedance of cochlear perilymph.

vis.alt: Chain of ossicles: tympanic membrane to malleus, incus and stapes footplate in the oval window, with tensor tympani on the malleus supplied by CN V3 and stapedius on the stapes supplied by CN VII.
vis.caption: Sound passes membrane, malleus, incus, stapes; two small muscles dampen loud sound.

steps.tx: Two muscles protect the auditory apparatus from acoustic trauma. The **tensor tympani** arises from the cartilaginous auditory tube and inserts onto the malleus handle. It is innervated by the mandibular nerve. The **stapedius muscle** arises from the pyramidal eminence and inserts onto the stapes neck. It is innervated by the facial nerve. Stapedius paralysis in Bell palsy produces hyperacusis.

steps.tx: The **cochlear duct** houses the organ of Corti within the bony cochlea. Perilymph fills the scala vestibuli and scala tympani, having high sodium like extracellular fluid. Endolymph fills the scala media, secreted by the stria vascularis with high potassium concentration. Deflection of stereocilia against the tectorial membrane opens mechanosensitive potassium channels, depolarizing inner hair cells and transmitting impulses via the vestibulocochlear nerve.
